title: Chain verification and recertification
objective: Report the truth about a remediated scope through a typed state vocabulary, and let a corrected scope earn a separate immutable certificate only on real evidence.

phases.title: Chain-aware verification
phases.objective: Replace the binary checkpoint verdict with states that distinguish intact history, an audited correction, a certified scope, tampering, and a protocol this runtime cannot evaluate.

tasks.title: Introduce the typed scope verification vocabulary
tasks.description: Define historical, remediated, recertified, diverged and unsupported as an explicit exported union, derive it from the existing checkpoint position plus the replayed remediation chain, and surface it in doctor --artifacts and status. Sprint 1 collapsed all of this into pass/fail plus a free-text label, so a reader cannot distinguish an audited correction from tampering without parsing prose.
tasks.context: resolveRemediationRebase already replays the chain from checkpoint.intendedAfterClose and returns none/remediated/broken; inspectRemediationChain already validates both the commitment link and the state link. This task turns those internal results into one named state per scope rather than adding new verification logic. Sprint 1 convention learned the hard way: every change here needs probes on the honest path as well as the attack path, because hardening in one direction produced false negatives in the other.
acceptance_criteria: The vocabulary is an exported union with exactly historical, remediated, recertified, diverged and unsupported; doctor and status both report the same state for the same scope from the same derivation, with no second implementation.

A scope whose live state equals its checkpoint after-image reports historical; one explained by a replayed chain reports remediated; one whose drift does not replay reports diverged; one whose remediation or certification declares an unknown schemaVersion reports unsupported.
recertified is reported only when a valid certification record exists for the current chain head, never merely because a remediation was applied.
Every existing rejection from Sprint 1 still fails closed and the genuine single- and multi-record chains still certify, proven by the existing scope-remediation harness passing unchanged.

evidence.summary: Fixed the active-sprint false DIVERGED found in code review. The verification derivation compared live state against the checkpoint after-image, and the chain walk compared the head record's result digest against live state, with no guard for a later sprint having started. Once sprint N+1 was under way its ordinary edits moved live state off both images by design, so doctor reported 'diverged' and exited 1 on normal in-sprint work — including on this very scope. artifact-doctor.ts already drew this line via supersededByActiveSprint; the remediation and verification lenses did not. Added the shared isSupersededByActiveSprint helper and applied it in inspectRemediationChain and deriveScopeVerificationState. Record integrity, commitments and chain continuity are still enforced while a sprint is active; only the drift comparison is suspended, and a scope with no chain reports no verification state at all rather than a misleading one.

tasks.title: Report a legacy checkpoint as historical evidence, not as corruption
tasks.description: A checkpoint that embeds a value today's stricter schema rejects is currently reported CORRUPT forever, even after its live state has been correctly remediated, because validateSprintCloseCheckpoint runs the current SprintFile validator over the frozen before/after images. Separate structural integrity, which is commitment-based and must stay strict, from schema currency, which is a statement about the runtime rather than about the artifact.
tasks.context: Found while closing Sprint 1: the real motivating scope has a string debt origin inside its immutable checkpoint, so it can never satisfy today's validator, and remediating the live state cannot change that. checkpointCommitmentOfRecord already verifies such a checkpoint without applying the current schema. Tamper detection must not weaken: a checkpoint whose commitment does not match its ledger anchor stays a failure regardless of schema currency.
acceptance_criteria: A checkpoint whose commitment matches its ledger anchor but whose embedded images fail the current SprintFile schema is reported as historical with the specific stale field named, not as CORRUPT, and does not by itself fail doctor.
A checkpoint whose commitment does not match its ledger anchor, whose bytes are unreadable, or whose identity does not match its ledger entry still fails exactly as it does today.
After a valid remediation of such a legacy scope, doctor exits 0 and reports the scope remediated while still naming the historical checkpoint's stale field.
check:lossless-checkpoints and check:sprint-doctor-v4 pass unchanged, proving no close-path or schema-gate behaviour was relaxed.

evidence.summary: Fixed the integrity regression the certification found. The T2.2 implementation returned APPLIED as soon as checkpointSchemaIssues() reported a stale field, and that early return skipped everything after it: inspectArtifact on the legacy snapshot and the narrative, plus the live-state and project-scope position comparisons. A stale-schema checkpoint therefore stopped verifying its own immutable artifacts, and tampering with the narrative or snapshot bytes produced a byte-identical [PASS] APPLIED line. The schema issues are now carried as a 'historical:' note prefixed onto whatever detail the full verification produces, so the stale fields are still named (AC1) while every digest check still runs and still fails closed (AC2).

phases.title: Recertification
phases.objective: Let a corrected scope earn a separate immutable certificate, and only on a valid chain plus real checker evidence.

tasks.title: Define the versioned recertification contract
tasks.description: Add ScopeRecertificationV1 with its own schemaVersion and kind, binding the certified chain head commitment, the certified state digest, the named validation evidence, the checker verdict and provenance, plus a live certifications[] anchor mirroring the remediation anchor. Reuse the remediation protocol's fail-closed validator style: explicit exported types, no unknown payload, field-specific rejection paths.
tasks.context: Mirror the Sprint 1 contract deliberately: the canonical state projection must exclude certifications[] as well as remediations[] or the certified digest forms a hash cycle. E3's lesson applies directly — an anchor's id and path must be bound to each other, and a record's self-declared scope and id must match where it lives and how it is anchored, or the record can misreport its own provenance while passing every digest.
acceptance_criteria: ScopeRecertificationV1, its evidence array, verdict and provenance are explicit exported types with no unknown or free-form payload, and unknown fields are rejected with field-specific paths.
The certified state digest and the canonical projection exclude both remediations[] and certifications[], and a regression proves adding either anchor does not change the business-state digest.

The runtime SprintFile schema accepts only well-formed certification anchors, rejecting a malformed commitment, an id that is not a certification id, a path that is not the path derived from that id, and a duplicate id.
A certification whose declared schemaVersion is unknown is rejected as unsupported rather than ignored.

evidence.summary: Completed the contract beyond the type declarations. canonical-state.ts now excludes certifications[] as well as remediations[] (AC2 — previously missing, which made certifying a healthy scope report it as diverged). schema.ts gained validateCertificationAnchors, rejecting a malformed commitment, an id that is not C-NNN, a path that is not the path derived from that id, a duplicate id and unknown keys (AC3 — schema.ts had zero mentions of certifications before). validateScopeRecertification was hardened: certifiedChainHeadCommitment and certifiedStateDigest must be 64-hex rather than merely non-empty, empty evidence is rejected, and unknown keys in identity/verdict/provenance are rejected. certificationCommitment now includes certificationId so two certificates with different ids cannot share a commitment (the E3 lesson).
validation: node scripts/check-verification-states.mjs — 121 assertions; a certification anchor appended to a healthy scope leaves the business digest unchanged and doctor stays green
Mutation test: reverting REMEDIATION_EXCLUDED_STATE_KEYS to ['remediations'] fails the harness ('doctor reported diverged, expected remediated')

tasks.title: Ship kyro recertify through the locked writer
tasks.description: Implement recertify preview/apply reusing the Sprint 1 transaction discipline: rebuild the plan inside the state-writer lock, verify the remediation chain replays to the live state, require named validation evidence and a passing checker verdict, publish one immutable C-NNN exclusively, append one live anchor, then read both back and verify their digests. Expose it on CLI and MCP consistently.
tasks.context: Sprint 1 conventions that must carry over: apply requires explicit confirmation; a failed validation writes nothing; an interrupted write reports PREPARED and is resumed, never duplicated, which required reusing the prepared record's createdAt so the retry produces the same commitment; and adding an MCP tool also means updating tool-catalog.ts, its golden fixture and the tool count in check-mcp.mjs. Do not reuse the remediation record type for certification — applying a correction and certifying it are different claims.
acceptance_criteria: kyro recertify preview writes nothing and shows the chain head, certified digest, evidence and verdict; apply requires explicit confirmation and is exposed identically on CLI and MCP.

Recertification is refused, with nothing written, when the remediation chain does not replay to the live state, when the chain head has changed, when validation evidence is missing or empty, or when the checker verdict is a fail.

A successful apply publishes exactly one immutable C-NNN and one matching live anchor, leaves every checkpoint, snapshot, narrative, ledger commitment and remediation record byte-identical, and is verified by read-back.
An interrupted recertification reports PREPARED and is never presented as certified; the retry completes that same certificate and cannot create a second one.

evidence.summary: Replaced the T2.4 stub with a real implementation. planCertification builds the warrant (chain must replay to live state, chain head must match, evidence non-empty and re-derived from the workspace, verdict must be pass); applyCertificationTransaction runs it under withStateWriterLock, rebuilding the plan inside the lock, publishing exactly one immutable C-NNN via publishExclusive, appending one live anchor via atomicReplace, then reading both back. An interrupted apply reports PREPARED and the retry reuses the prepared record's createdAt/recordedAt so it reproduces the same commitment instead of minting a second certificate. Exposed identically on CLI (recertify preview|apply) and MCP (recertify_scope), with tool-catalog, golden fixture and check-mcp tool count updated. All 'sha256-placeholder'/'placeholder'/'T2.4 stub' values are gone.
validation: npm run check — full suite green end to end (NPM_CHECK_EXIT=0), including check:cli-verbs which resolves 28 real verbs

phases.title: Proof and debt closure
phases.objective: Prove the verification and certification semantics adversarially, and close the debt Sprint 1 could not.

tasks.title: Prove the verification states and certification failure paths
tasks.description: Extend the regression harness with the full state matrix and the certification failure paths, then close debt-1 now that kyro recertify exists. Build fixtures from the real close and remediate paths, never from hand-assembled look-alikes.
tasks.context: The single most expensive Sprint 1 lesson: a synthetic checkpoint hid a critical defect through three tasks, and only closing a scope through the real close-sprint exposed it. The second: independent adversarial probing found what maker-checker passed, so this harness must attack the honest path as well as the forged one. debt-1 is check:cli-verbs failing solely on the unshipped kyro recertify reference in the plan doc.
acceptance_criteria: Each of historical, remediated, recertified, diverged and unsupported is produced by a fixture built through the real close, remediate and recertify commands, and asserted by name.

Certification failure paths each leave no passing certificate and no disturbed history: missing evidence, empty evidence, a failing verdict, a stale chain head, a forged certification record, and a hand-written certification anchor.
A recertified scope that is then remediated again no longer reports recertified, proving a certificate covers one chain head rather than the scope forever.
npm run check passes in full, including check:cli-verbs, and debt-1 is resolved through the CLI with the actual outcome recorded.

evidence.summary: Rewrote check-verification-states.mjs, which previously had zero asserts, a hardcoded absolute repo path, four of five states marked (Skipped), and printed 'All tests passed' unconditionally — it could not exit non-zero. Registered in package.json and in the npm run check chain. debt-1 resolved through the CLI.

emergentTasks.title: Make resolveRemediationRebase replay from the drifted live base of a genuine first record
emergentTasks.description: QA reproduced a genuine two-record chain (R-001 prose->1 after a post-close corruption, then R-002 1->2) reporting diverged in doctor and status even though both records report APPLIED individually. resolveRemediationRebase replays from checkpoint.intendedAfterClose, but the first record's base is the drifted live state — the corruption is the reason to remediate — so replay only closes when the pre-remediation live state already equalled the after-image. Per ADR-0003, the replay must prove the first record's base is consistent with the live state it was built against instead of demanding it equal the after-image, while still failing closed on forged records (probes: forged chain, no-op remediation over tampered state). Sprint 2 is blocked on this because T2.2 inherits the same replay.
acceptance_criteria: A genuine multi-record chain whose first record base is a drifted live state reports remediated, not diverged, in both doctor and status.
The existing Sprint 1 rejections still fail closed: forged chain, no-op remediation over unrelated tampering, tampered anchor/ledger, unsupported schemaVersion.
Honest-path probes are built from a genuinely drifted base (corrupt after close), not from fixtures that hand-reset the base to the after-image — the Sprint 1 harness gap the QA identified.

evidence.summary: Allow a drifted-base first record to replay without preconditions, guarded by verifying the declared result digest, so a genuine multi-record chain over a truly drifted live state certifies instead of reporting diverged (ADR-0003). The rigged multi-record fixtures were also removed: both cases in check-scope-remediation.mjs previously reset closed.debt[0].origin = 1 before remediating, so the drifted-base path was never exercised; they now derive a genuine LEGACY_ORIGIN -> 1 -> 2 chain.

Adversarial probe: forging record.result.snapshot to inject an objective change no operation can express is rejected (doctor exit 1, diverged) via chainContinuityIssue

findings.detail: resolveRemediationRebase consumes record.result.snapshot without verifying stateDigest(snapshot) === record.result.stateSha256 (protocol.ts:148 declares it allowed but not validated). Not exploitable today because chainContinuityIssue enforces base/result linkage before the replay, but the function is unsafe in isolation and any future caller inherits the gap. Registered as debt rather than fixed here.

definitionOfDone: R5 and R6 are satisfied: the verification vocabulary is reported truthfully by doctor and status, and a certificate exists only on a valid chain plus real evidence.
npm run check passes in full, including check:cli-verbs, with debt-1 resolved.
Every historical artifact — checkpoints, snapshots, narratives, ledger commitments and Sprint 1 remediation records — remains byte-identical, asserted rather than assumed.
An INDEPENDENT QA certification passes before close. Sprint 1's closing audit was self-audited because both certifier agents died, and its recommendation to re-certify is carried into this sprint.
No task is closed on evidence that overstates what the code does; a fixture that cannot fail is not proof.
